newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel recurring Q1 net up by 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel recurring Q1 net up by 25 pct.

text.p: San Miguel Corp said on Tuesday that strong earnings from its liquor and real estate businesses and a recovery in the food sector boosted recurring net income by 25 percent in the first quarter to 904 million pesos.
The company reported a net income of 725 million pesos in the first quarter last year.
The food and beer giant said this partly offset weaker profits from beer and soft drinks.

San Miguel reported on Tuesday it total net income of 1.11 billion pesos in the first quarter compared with 781 million pesos in the same period last year. The 1997 first quarter figure included a net one-time gain of 207 million pesos from the sale of an old brewery site in Jakarta.

Sales volume in the food and packaging business increased by four and eight percent, respectively. However, these were offset by a one percent decline in volumes in the beverage segment, San Miguel said.

Domestic beer sales fell after price increases were implemented in March to cover for increased taxes. This brought down volume growth in beer to five percent in the entire first quarter after eight percent growth in the first two months.
The operating income of San Miguel's beer operations fell by 39 percent to 563 million pesos from 921 million, the company said.

Overseas, San Miguel's beer volumes grew by 15 percent in Hong Kong and China and more than doubled in Vietnam. But as a result of intensified spending on distribution and brand development efforts, San Miguel's international operations posted an operating loss of 360 million pesos.
Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, its 70 percent-owned unit, had a first quarter sales revenue of 5.63 billion pesos from 5.51 billion pesos year-ago.
Its operating income, however, went down by 17 percent to 602 million pesos in the first quarter from 729 million as sales volume was flat compared with year-ago levels.
Coca-Cola Bottlers is being sold to Australian-based soft drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd in exchange for a 25 percent stake in Amatil.

Among the big income contributors, La Tondena Distillers Inc posted a 21 percent increase in sales revenue to 2.48 billion pesos from 2.05 billion due to higher prices and sales volume of liquor and mineral water.

Sales revenue of the food and agribusiness segment, including San Miguel's share in Nestle Philippines Inc, improved by 14 percent to 12.2 billion pesos. Operating income of the segment rose by nine percent to 741 million pesos.
San Miguel Properties Philippines Inc produced a net profit of 671 million pesos in the first quarter compared worth 120 million in the year-earlier quarter.
The firm said the growth in real estate income mostly came from the sale of shares in HOC Realty Inc, a unit established to redevelop San Miguel's head office site.
